Nadia: Heads-up — quick P95 jump in us-west-2 rack-21 at 09:04. A bunch of fractional dedicated allocations got nudged and then spilled into shared pools.
Omar: saw it. Any obvious IO/egress culprits?
Nadia: NVLINK write latency + host PCIe stall counters spike. NIC tx bursts right after. Looks like a host-local IO storm, not a network fabric issue.
Bea: those hosts have recent best-effort transforms from nightly batch group D. Could be a co-located heavy job.
Sanjay: immediate mitigations: (1) apply a temporary egress pacer to best-effort cgroup on rack-21 hosts, (2) mark the host set as "hotspot-avoid" in allocator for 20m, (3) raise requeue cooldown for allocations coming off those hosts to 120s.
Nadia: agree. We should also avoid flipping routing policies broadly; do a 10% allocator canary for the avoid-label so we don't thrash.
Omar: commands I plan to run:
```
fleetctl run --hosts rack-21 "ebpf-pacer --cgroup best-effort --egress 45% --tag incident-3210007777"
kubectl patch cm allocator-policy -n fleet -p '{"data":{"hotspot_avoid_canary":"0.10","hotspot_avoid_rack21":"true"}}'
```
Bea: add a short-lived metric panel for "pci_write_stalls", "nvlink_write_latency", and "requeue_cooldown_rate" in the Dedicated -> preemptions dashboard.
oncall-bot: egress pacer scheduled on 5 hosts in rack-21.
Sanjay: applied egress pacer. nvlink_latency down ~28% in 90s, pci_write_stalls down ~22% in 2m. Preempts reduced but we still see some requeues into rack-21.
Nadia: good initial signal. Does allocator honor the hotspot_avoid_canary?
Omar: yes, canary 10% active. requeue_same_host_count down ~35% after 7m. P95 improved ~45ms.
Bea: caveat: a couple of high-state tenants got moved and saw KV warmup, small error bump on long tail. We should tag sticky tenants and exclude them from automatic moves for 30m.
Sanjay: adding a temporary sticky label for those tenant IDs and noting in the incident doc. Also creating ticket INF-8421 to evaluate a less aggressive auto-evict for stateful tenants.
Nadia: plan: keep pacer + canary for 20m, track nvlink/pci/nic metrics + requeue_same_host_count. If stable after 20m, remove pacer and instead schedule batch jobs away from rack-21 for the next 6 hours while we investigate.
Omar: will instrument a reactive alert for nvlink > 80% for 90s and requeue_same_host_count > 5/min.
Bea: I'll draft a short runbook note: when nvlink+pcie stall pattern appears, prefer host-level pacer + allocator avoid canary before applying global routing changes.
Nadia: thanks team. I'll update the incident board with timeline. :thumbsup:
